what: How the tables relate to each other
title: 7. Tutorial: Parse an entire HPA xml file into relational tibbles with hpaXmlParse()
text: Unlike straight translation xml tree nested R lists (, schema, mean digging 6-7 levels deep reach single value), hpaXmlParse() normalizes everything flat, single-level list tibbles – similar small relational database extracted xml file: Every row, except single top-level entry row, carries foreign key column "<parent>_id" pointing back row (another tibble) belongs . Tibbles nested entities (entry, data, patient, image, antibody, …) additionally surrogate key column "<name>_id", children point . Tibbles leaf/property elements (tissueCell_level, patient_location, …) never referenced anything, carry parent’s foreign key . leaf/property tibble, element’s text content sits column literally named value, xml attributes keep names columns. leaf element schema guarantees can never repeat gets tibble : merged parent’s row, text content column named tag (’s CCNB1$entry name column rather separate entry_name table) attributes columns named "<tag>_<attribute>". example, CCNB1$tissueCell rows carry data_id matches data_id parent row CCNB1$data, CCNB1$tissueCell_level rows carry tissueCell_id pointing back CCNB1$tissueCell: xml tags mean different things depending appear – level staining intensity tissueCell RNA abundance data; location appears tissueCell patient. keep tables unambiguous, kind leaf/property-style element named "<parent>_<tag>" (tissueCell_level, patient_location, tissueCell_cellType, …). Bigger nested entities represent “kind record” wherever occur – image, data, patient, antibody, – keep plain tag name disambiguated foreign key columns instead (e.g. rows CCNB1$image came antibody’s western blot carry westernBlot_id, rows tissue assay carry tissueExpression_id).
